comparison: Perfect alignment on pH-dependence findings (C84-C94). Both evaluations accept the quantitative pH-dependent activity data and structural similarity across pH values. OpenEval emphasizes the maintained high correlation (R² > 0.95) between metal binding and product formation, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the rigorous evidence for the concerted mechanism.

Disagreement on monovalent ion findings (C75, C77-C80). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to crystal deterioration preventing high-concentration Tl⁺ soaking during reaction, noting transient binding cannot be definitively ruled out. Peer reviewers SUPPORT these findings as part of evidence for single metal ion mechanism, accepting that no additional metal ions were found despite sensitive methods.

Strong agreement on time-resolved crystallography approach and single metal ion mechanism (C45, C60-C74). Both evaluations affirm the experimental approach and results. Peer reviewers initially requested clarification about terminology (structures vs intermediates) which was addressed in revision, showing acceptance of data with appropriate description.

Agreement on concerted mechanism (C114-C121, C140-C149). Both evaluations support the coupling between metal binding and deprotonation. OpenEval acknowledges some mechanistic interpretation involves speculation about electrostatic coupling but finds experimental observations strong. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the concerted process conclusion based on quantitative correlations and mutant data.

Agreement on DNA pre-alignment and mechanistic distinctiveness (C131-C135, C129-C130, C137). Both evaluations support structural observations and the distinction from other nucleases. OpenEval notes C135's interpretation about transition state stabilization is somewhat speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers accept the unique mechanistic features and distinctiveness claims.

Agreement on mutagenesis data showing His98 as primary and His78 as alternative proton acceptor (C96-C107, C109-C110). Both evaluations accept the systematic mutagenesis results and activity trends. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative pKa shifts and imidazole rescue experiments. Peer reviewers accept mutational effects as part of rigorous evidence.

Agreement on multiple deprotonation pathways (C100, C107, C111-C112). Both evaluations support findings about alternative pathways. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative evidence from mutagenesis. Peer reviewers accept this as providing 'new insight into the catalytic mechanism' and note the study validates multiple aspects of the mechanism.

Agreement on imidazole rescue experiments (C108-C110). Both evaluations support the finding that double histidine mutant retains residual activity rescued by exogenous imidazole. OpenEval notes authors acknowledge inability to observe imidazole binding in crystallo. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the mutagenesis evidence.

Agreement on H98A mutant's effect on metal binding (C114-C115, C117-C118). Both evaluations support the surprising finding that His98 mutation affects Mg²⁺ binding despite no direct interaction. OpenEval emphasizes this as evidence for concerted mechanism. Peer reviewers find this 'interesting' and worthy of future investigation, explicitly accepting the finding.

Agreement on single metal ion mechanism (C46, C76, C128). Both evaluations strongly support this central finding. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple approaches and strong quantitative correlations. Peer reviewers describe the demonstration as 'convincing' with all three reviewers explicitly affirming this finding.

Agreement on structural comparisons distinguishing I-PpoI from multi-metal-ion enzymes (C129-C130, C137). Both evaluations support these structural observations. OpenEval notes these are direct observations from crystallographic data. Peer reviewers accept the distinctiveness and unique mechanistic features of I-PpoI.

OpenEval evaluated background and prior knowledge claims (C1-C44) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory/background claims.
